title: Uncertainty-aware Causal Decision Making via Effect Bound Decomposition
abstract: arXiv:2601.22736v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Causal inference from observational data can provide strong evidence for finding the best action in a decision-making scenario without having to perform expensive randomized trials. The causal effect of an action is often not pointwise identifiable even with infinite data due to unobserved confounding factors. Furthermore, having only finitely many samples adds another layer of uncertainty to causal effect estimation. Several existing methods can be used to obtain upper and lower bounds to the causal effect, ranging from symbolic methods to the more recent neural network-based approaches, which implicitly incorporate both sources of uncertainty. However, these methods do not inform whether collecting more samples may or may not help identify the best action from observational data, leaving experts in the dark about their data collection strategies. translated_title: 基于效应界分解的不确定性感知因果决策
translated_abstract: 基于观测数据的因果推断可以为决策场景中寻找最佳行动提供有力证据，而无需进行昂贵的随机化试验。由于存在未观测的混杂因素，即使拥有无限数据，一个行动的因果效应通常也无法进行逐点识别。此外，仅有有限数量的样本又为因果效应估计增加了另一层不确定性。现有多种方法可用于获得因果效应的上界和下界，从符号方法到较新的基于神经网络的方法，这些方法隐式地融合了上述两种不确定性来源。然而，这些方法无法告知专家收集更多样本是否有助于从观测数据中识别最佳行动，使专家对其数据收集策略一无所知。我们通过一个新颖的框架来解决这一问题，该框架能够区分……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了一种新颖的效应界分解框架，能够将因果效应不确定性区分为不可约简的混杂不确定性与可通过增加样本量约简的采样不确定性，从而指导专家判断收集更多数据是否有助于识别最佳行动。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a novel effect bound decomposition framework that distinguishes irreducible confounding uncertainty from reducible sampling uncertainty in causal effect bounds, thereby guiding experts on whether collecting more observational data can help identify the best action.
